descripcion_geo: Small Aramaic kingdom southwest of Hermon, adjacent to Geshur. Mentioned in the conquest of Joshua and in the David wars.
importancia_estrategica: Aramaic kingdom next to Hermon; David did not conquer it; Its inhabitants were occasional allies of Israel's enemies.

historias.titulo: Maacá was not conquered by Israel
historias.descripcion: Maacá and Gesur were left unconquered in the Joshua campaign; Its inhabitants lived among the Israelites.

historias.titulo: The Ammonites hire Maacah against David
historias.descripcion: The Ammonites hire the army of Maacah and Zobah to confront David in their war.
Maacah, Absalom's mother, was the daughter of the king of Geshur; The region of Maacah was united to Geshur.

personajes.descripcion: He left Maacah unconquered; its inhabitants persisted on the land.
He fought against the army of Maacah hired by the Ammonites.
Name of the Gesureo-Maacathite princess who married David.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Maacá: relevant geographical region in the Old Testament.

judaismo.descripcion: Unconquered lands like Maacah and Geshur are signs of incomplete obedience in Deuteronomic theology: what is not eliminated ends up being a trap.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Unconquered lands like Maacah and Geshur are signs of incomplete obedience in Deuteronomic theology: what is not eliminated ends up being a trap.
